name: Coastal Dhofari Arabic

ancestors.notes: Omani Arabic base; this leaf declares only the jim range.

notes:
Coastal Dhofari Arabic, the Arabic of Salalah and the Dhofar coast of southern Oman. INPUT CONTRACT: transcribes orthography+harakat. It hangs off ar-OM and declares one delta, which is a range rather than a value.

ج jīm is THREE READINGS because the coastal plain holds three coexisting sociolects that disagree about it. Davey 2013 table 2.34 (thesis pp.52-53) separates them: Group 1, the monolingual historic coastal community and the thesis's actual object of study, reads jīm [ɡ]; Group 2, bilingual in Sheḥri or Mehri and of mountain origin, reads [dʒ]; Group 3, migrants of Nejd and highland origin around Shisr and Thumrait, reads [dʒ] or [j], a pattern Davey says is 'attested to in Ḥaḍrāmi Arabic'. All three are listed, Group 1 first because it is the described variety, and the lattice carries the others rather than a choice being made on the reader's behalf. THIS IS NOT FREE VARIATION WITHIN ONE SPEAKER: it is three communities, and which one a recording belongs to is a fact about the speaker that the text cannot show.

ق qāf is INHERITED UNCHANGED and that is deliberate. Davey's Groups 1 and 2 read [q], Group 3 reads [ɡ], and ar-OM already offers ['q', 'ɡ'] in that order — the same range in the same order, so there is nothing to declare. The interdentals are likewise inherited: Davey p.38 names 'the retention of the interdentals /θ/, /ð/, and /ð̣/, as well as the voiceless uvular plosive /q/, which is rare outside of the region (Holes 2004: 81)', and the parent already retains them.

NOT MODELLED. Davey p.38 reports imāla, word-final vowel raising, 'which local speakers consider to be the most prominent feature of their language' — no rule is declared for it here because the thesis gives it as a salient impression rather than a stated environment, and a rule invented to fit would be this file's guess wearing a citation. Kaškaša with the 2FS suffix as [-iš] (p.100, citing al-Azraqi 2007:555-557) is a morphological fact about a suffix, not a grapheme reading.

CLASSIFICATION: Dhofari is Arabic and is not Modern South Arabian. Mehri, Sheḥri and Jibbali are separate Semitic languages in contact with it, and the Group 2 speakers above are bilingual in one of them; nothing in Davey treats Dhofari phonology as MSAL-derived. ISO adf, Glottolog dhof1235 — NOT acw, which is Hejazi.

PAGINATION WARNING: the page numbers above are the 2013 Manchester thesis's own, from the author's freely available PDF. The 2016 Brill edition is repaginated and these numbers will not match it.
